description: Exports that legitimately have no consumer INSIDE this repo, because they are the surface third parties call. Every entry carries a reason someone can disagree with — 'it's public API' is exactly the excuse that would let inert seams back in, so it has to be argued, not asserted.

packages.sdk: The dev-facing facade over the platform (CLAUDE.md invariant 5). Its whole job is to be called from outside this repo.
packages.core: The kernel — ports + kernel logic. Exports ports that adapters implement and apps compose; a port with no in-repo caller is the normal case, not a dead seam.
packages.transports: Concrete transport adapters behind the mesh builder. Published surface; apps reach them through the builder, never directly (the SURFACE rule).
packages.vault: Key/secret storage adapter. Published surface consumed via the SDK facade.
packages.pod-client: Solid-pod read/write/seal. Published surface; also consumed in-repo, so only its unreached half lands here.
packages.redaction: Redaction primitives — published so a third-party app can redact before export.
packages.pseudo-pod: The file-shaped pod stand-in. Published so an app can run pod-shaped without a pod.
packages.item-types: The canonical item-type schemas. Published BECAUSE third parties declare types against them.
packages.item-store: The per-circle store + sync seams. Published surface; the guard still governs its non-barrel internals.
packages.app-manifest: The manifest schema + projectors. Published — an app declaring a manifest is the primary third-party act.
packages.app-scaffold: Scaffolds a new app from a manifest. By definition only ever called from outside.
packages.attribute-charter: The requested-attributes charter vocabulary. Published so a consumer can state what it asks for.
packages.oidc-session: OIDC session handling for pod sign-in. Published adapter surface.
packages.agent-registry: Profiles, disclosure, endorsements. Published surface; several exports are the A2A card contract other agents read.

note: PLAN-sdk-publishing.md decides which packages are publishable: at/below the substrate layer AND part of the public API. This file records that decision where the guard can read it. If a package is added here, it is claiming to be publishable — check that plan first. Packages NOT listed here (secure-agent, mcp-bridge, llm-client, data-connectors, blob-gateway, pod-search, kring-host, recipe-loader, notifier, confidential-llm, versioning, agent-ui, chat-agent, circles, identity-resolver) are internal, and an unreached export in them is a real finding.
